title: United States and Ukraine sign minerals agreement creating Reconstruction Investment Fund
body:
On 30 April 2025, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Ukrainian Economy Minister and First Deputy Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko signed an agreement in Washington giving the United States access to Ukraine's rare minerals. The deal created the United States-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. The signing came two months after a planned signing was cancelled following the Oval Office confrontation between Presidents Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky on 28 February.

According to Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal, each side holds 50 percent of the voting rights in the fund, and profits are to be reinvested only in Ukraine. Svyrydenko said the fund would be financed exclusively by income from new licences, and that 50 percent of the income from critical materials and oil and gas projects would go to Ukraine's budget. The US Treasury and the US International Development Finance Corporation were to work with Kyiv to finalise governance.

The agreement states that all resources on Ukraine's territory and in its territorial waters belong to Ukraine, and that Kyiv alone decides where and what to extract. Shmyhal said Ukraine would not have to repay the billions of dollars in US weapons and support provided since February 2022.

The agreement contained no US security guarantees, which Ukrainian lawmaker Roman Kostenko said remained an open question. Bessent presented the deal as a signal to Russia of US commitment to a peace process. Ukraine's cabinet approved it on 30 April, and it still required ratification by the Ukrainian parliament.
